requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
2–5 years of experience in software quality engineering, with significant experience testing web applications.
Solid understanding of software testing principles, test design techniques, and the software development lifecycle.
Hands-on experience testing web applications across browsers, devices, and screen sizes, using browser developer tools to inspect network requests, console errors, and page behavior.
Experience developing and maintaining automated UI and API tests in Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, or similar frameworks.
Experience testing RESTful APIs with tools such as Postman or code-based test frameworks, and validating data using SQL.

responsibilities: TP-Link is seeking a Software Quality Assurance Engineer to join our Cloud Web Platforms Quality Engineering team. In this role, you will help ensure the quality of TP-Link's global websites, web applications, and AI-powered customer experiences, which reach millions of users across dozens of countries and languages.

This role is ideal for a quality engineer who enjoys both breadth and depth: someone comfortable moving between browser-based UI testing, backend API validation, and automation, and who wants to grow expertise across web and cloud technologies.

Develop risk-based test strategies and execute functional, integration, regression, and end-to-end testing for websites, web applications, content-management systems, APIs, and supporting cloud services.
Participate in requirements reviews and design discussions to clarify acceptance criteria, identify risks early, and improve product testability.

Build and maintain automated UI and API tests using Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript and frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or equivalent tools. Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.
Validate backend APIs, service integrations, database behavior, and data integrity using API tools, code-based test frameworks, and SQL.
Investigate failures and isolate root causes using browser developer tools, network traces, application logs, system telemetry, and database queries.
